correctness.rationale: The full pointwise transfer lemma is valid for every subdomain containing every constant function: at a fixed state, any M-witness to an existential matrix formula can be represented by the constant function with that value; induction over the formula therefore commutes with all quantifiers. This gives truth value all states for every ZFC axiom and scheme instance. GCH makes 2^lambda=lambda^+. For lambda>=kappa, a function with coordinate lambda at one state and lambda^+ elsewhere lies in the size cut (internal cardinality of tc(lambda) is lambda), and both coordinatewise strict box inequalities hold since M contains at least two states. For lambda<kappa, any nonconstant cardinal-valued function admitted by the size cut has every coordinate >=kappa, whereas a proposed interval member must have every coordinate <=lambda^+<=kappa; either impossible or forces the constant upper endpoint. These two cases exhaust all infinite cardinal lambda. Finite toy-state checks are only diagnostics of inequalities, not proofs of ZFC.
residual_risks: The result depends critically on Boolean pointwise semantics, not classical direct-product satisfaction.
Requires a transitive set model of ZFC+GCH; no claim of an actual transitive model existence from ZFC alone.

originality.rationale: Yago/Jockwich Martinez/Venturi, Models of Arbitrary Sets (arxiv:2610.23219), has a rank-cut strict threshold lambda>kappa (Props.4.9,4.10) and a general transfer lemma for all constant-containing subdomains (Prop.4.11), and explicitly proposes transitive-closure size cuts as future work in §5.3. The new size-cut domain and inclusive boundary lambda=kappa are not stated as a theorem there. Transfer yields the ZFC part but not the interval existential classification; the supplied witness and negative case prove the new threshold. This is a narrow, direct continuation of the primary work, not a claim of independent foundational discovery.
residual_risks: The size-cut example is explicitly suggested by the original paper, so its priority is narrow and tied to the as-yet-unstated threshold formula.
A general Boolean-valued interpolation principle may make this classification a simple corollary, but such an explicit stronger theorem was not located.

value.rationale: The primary set-theory paper explicitly proposes varying its cardinal filtration using transitive-closure size. The theorem completely settles, for this natural proposed filter, exactly which constant-cardinal power-set intervals admit crisp intermediates, including a boundary where its rank-cut analog gives the opposite answer. This is a motivated sharp filtration distinction even though the proof is short and does not claim a broad foundations breakthrough.
residual_risks: The inclusive boundary follows by a simple two-valued function, so significance is limited to a natural exact variant of the proposed filtration.

final_claim: For a transitive set model M of ZFC+GCH with infinite internal cardinal kappa, the constant-plus-transitive-closure-size>=kappa pointwise Boolean-valued domain models ZFC and has a crisp intermediate between delta(lambda) and delta(lambda)^power precisely when lambda>=kappa.
limitations: A specific transitive M of ZFC+GCH and one TC-size filter; not all filtrations or semantic models.
A set-theoretic existence statement, not a numerical computation.
